items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: out of Spike, the club owners just for Spike will cut the band down to five men.

ctx.x: I don't know. I think it was Bill Cray, somebody like that, or Leonard Ferguson, one of the guys, musicians that I've talked to, saying that all nightclub owners want to get rid of bass. They don't understand the importance of it, you know. No, I don't. And he was saying how important the bass is.

I don't agree with that. Not all nightclubers want to. I'll tell you where you might have misunderstood them. It's not the nightclub owners want to get rid of the bass. It's because to a band leader, your drum, bass, and piano are three important instruments. You're a foundation. We're supplying the bottom, and we're giving it the drive and the depth. And where you may have gotten the wrong opinion, usually when the unions raise the scale on these steady band leaders, and you have a six-piece band, and they're…
Well, some people just don't appreciate what good time is, either.
